pr_title: drivers: ethernet: w5500: fix the stack overflow
pr_body:
It will fix #46684. add the temporary rx buffer corresponding to the L2 frame MTU instead of dynamic array. add the sanity check for the L2 frame length. it will reopen the MACRAW socket when frame length is invalid and can't recover by RX_RSR.
[Update]~~Also it changes(fixes) the disabling interrupt by writing 0 to SIMR register as datasheet.~~

Signed-off-by: Pengxiang Gao <honestech74@gmail.com>

issue_context.title: ethernet: w5500: driver will be stack overflowed when reading the invalid(corrupt) packet length
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The current w5500 driver will halt(BUS FAULT or MPU FAULT) when reading the bad frame length. I am not sure if it's when there is some noise on SPI lines or when reading the invalid frame length somehow.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using?
    `nrf52840-dk` and `w5500` module
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
    workaround: allocate the maximum temporary buffer for reading and check if the frame length is valid(range in payload length of the ethernet frame - L2).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
It's hard to reproduce it but it happens anyway. I checked it with someone on Discord([#network](https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/985958672649834636)).
- upload any network example
- put the board in the LAN with lots of traffic and try to ping with big packet and short interval
- it might take a few hours or days

**Expected behavior**
It should work without any issue or recover even though there is any noise in the SPI lines or reading the invalid reg values from the chip.

**Impact**
It can occur two kinds of stack overflow for net_pkt and w5500_thread.
- when it tries to allocate larger buffer than `CONFIG_NET_RX_STACK_SIZE`
- when it tries to allocate larger buffer than `CONFIG_ETH_W5500_RX_THREAD_STACK_SIZE`

review_comments: Creating a new `define`, such as `ETH_PACKET_HEADER_LEN`, for substituting the [magic numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) `3` and `2` throughout this driver would be a welcome change for the readability I believe. To me, it's not clear what the `3` is meant to be.
Added the definitions for them and updated the prefix `MAC` to `ETH`.
